newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes quiet in Asia, focus on Minas, Duri glut.
newsitem.headline: Crudes quiet in Asia, focus on Minas, Duri glut.

text.p: Crude oil prices in Asia hovered in a narrow range in dull trade on Monday, while the physical market focused on the glut in Minas and Duri cargoes.
Cash April Brent was notionally assessed at $19.80/19.90, a touch higher than late U.S. trading levels on Friday of $19.75/19.85.
April Brent on SIMEX was untraded at 0740 GMT, and was indicated at $19.85/19.93, compared with London's IPE settlement of $19.86 on Friday. The SIMEX contract was range-bound throughout the day.
At 0745 GMT, April NYMEX light crude was indicated at $21.10/21.24 on the ACCESS after hours system, compared with New York's settlement of $21.28 on Friday, where it gained 34 cents.

In physical trading for Gulf crudes, Masila appeared to be the only April cargo still left on the market. Market participants said active trading would probably begin later this week after price negotiations for the second quarter were concluded. Most traders said the market for April Masila was mostly balanced with buying interest likely to emerge from South Korea and China.
